How do I get from Surat Thani airport to Koh Samui? | Buy a combo coach-and-ferry ticket at the desks in the arrivals hall (330–850 THB with Phantip, Raja, Lomprayah or Boonsiri); it takes about 3–4 hours to Nathon or Lipa Noi, and the last combos leave about 16:00.
How long is the ferry from Donsak to Koh Samui? | The Raja and Seatran car ferries take about 1.5 hours, and the Lomprayah, Boonsiri and Songserm catamarans take about 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Raja Ferry or Seatran: which is better? | Raja runs the longest hours (about 05:00–19:00), has the cheaper foot fare (220 THB against Seatran's 250 THB since April 2026) and lands at Lipa Noi, which suits the west and south; Seatran lands in Nathon town with more onward transport.
What time is the last ferry to Koh Samui? | The last Raja car ferry leaves Donsak at about 19:00; the last catamaran is Songserm at about 16:30, and the last combo tickets leave Surat Thani airport at about 16:00.
Can I buy the ferry ticket at the pier? | Yes, both Raja and Seatran sell tickets at their Donsak terminals for foot passengers and vehicles, and booking ahead is only worth it for peak weeks such as 20 December–5 January.
Where does the ferry arrive on Koh Samui? | Seatran, Lomprayah, Boonsiri and Songserm boats from Donsak arrive at Nathon pier on the west coast; Raja Ferry arrives at its own port at Lipa Noi, a few kilometres south.
Is there a night boat from Surat Thani to Koh Samui? | Not in 2026; the night boats from Surat Thani town serve Koh Phangan and Koh Tao, so for Samui take the last Raja ferry at about 19:00 or stay overnight.
Can I take my rental car on the ferry? | The ferries carry cars (about 730 THB or more including the driver on Seatran since April 2026), but many mainland rental contracts exclude ferry crossings and island use, so check your contract first.
